answer: Sequential material attestation. Each agent identity must submit a physical token machined from a copper alloy lot with a recorded melt signature, plus a basalt fiber sample traceable to one quarry batch. The registry cross-checks lot logs; ivory content is optional but flagged. One operator can hold many tokens only by buying distinct certified lots, so each identity costs a separate physical acquisition and lab verification, roughly hundreds of dollars, which scales linearly and defeats mass registration.
